topics.description_de: arguably, to some extent, it could be argued
second, third und mixed conditionals, wish
Vermutung und Kritik in der Vergangenheit (must have, should have)
present perfect, past perfect, used to, Zukunftsformen

topics.name_de: Deutsche Wörter und Strukturen im englischen Text

topics.description_de: make a decision, take into account, carry out
depend on, be responsible for, look forward to

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Hervorhebung mit what-Satz oder all-Satz: What I need is a holiday. All I want is some peace.
grammar_rules.example_positive: What I really need is a long holiday.
grammar_rules.example_negative: I really need a long holiday.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Kurze Adjektive mit -er/-est (cheaper, the cheapest), lange mit more/most (more expensive). Vergleich mit than.
Unzählbare Nomen haben keinen Plural (information, advice, furniture); people und police stehen mit dem Plural (people are).
Aussagen vorsichtig formulieren: It could be argued that …, to some extent, arguably, it seems that …, tend to.

patterns: \b(?:it could be argued|it can be argued|arguably|to some extent|to a certain extent|to a large extent|it would seem|it seems that|it appears that|is likely to|are likely to|presumably)\b

grammar_rules.example_positive: It could be argued that remote work increases productivity.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Am Satzanfang nach never, rarely, not only, no sooner, under no circumstances … folgt Fragewortstellung: Not only did she win, she also broke the record.
grammar_rules.example_positive: Not only did she win the race, she also broke the record.
grammar_rules.example_negative: She not only won the race, she also broke the record.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Vergangene Bedingung, gegenwärtige Folge: If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.
grammar_rules.example_positive: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Tokyo now.
grammar_rules.example_negative: If I take that job, I will live in Tokyo.

grammar_rules.title_de: Modalverb + have + Partizip (must have, should have)
grammar_rules.explanation_de: Vermutung oder Kritik über die Vergangenheit: She must have forgotten. You should have told me. They might have missed the bus.
grammar_rules.example_positive: You should have told me earlier.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Verben und Adjektive werden zu Nomen: because prices increased → due to the increase in prices; it is important → the importance of.
be + Partizip: Die Handlung steht im Mittelpunkt. The bridge was built in 1890. English is spoken here. Der Handelnde mit by.
grammar_rules.example_positive: The museum was built in the nineteenth century.
grammar_rules.example_negative: They built the museum in the nineteenth century.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: had + Partizip: was vor einem anderen Ereignis in der Vergangenheit geschah. When we arrived, the film had already started.
grammar_rules.example_positive: When we arrived, the film had already started.
grammar_rules.example_negative: When we arrived, the film started.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Abgeschlossene Handlung zu einem bestimmten Zeitpunkt: I went to London last year. Fragen und Verneinung mit did: Did you see it? I didn't see it.
have/has + Partizip: Erfahrungen und Handlungen mit Bezug zur Gegenwart (I have been to Rome. She has just left). Mit since/for für Dauer bis jetzt.
grammar_rules.example_positive: I have never seen such a beautiful view.
grammar_rules.example_negative: I never saw such a beautiful view.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Denselben Inhalt formell und informell ausdrücken: We regret to inform you … ↔ Sorry, but …
who für Personen, which für Dinge, that für beides in notwendigen Relativsätzen; whose für Besitz. Nicht notwendige Relativsätze mit Komma, ohne that.
Nach said/told/asked verschiebt sich die Zeit meist zurück: She said she was tired. He told me he would call.
grammar_rules.example_positive: She told me she would call later.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Hypothetische Bedingung in der Gegenwart: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese. Im if-Satz kein would.
grammar_rules.example_positive: If I had more money, I would travel around the world.
grammar_rules.example_negative: If I have more money, I will travel around the world.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: Das treffende Wort statt eines allgemeinen: mitigate statt make smaller, scrutinise statt look at, exacerbate statt make worse.

grammar_rules.title_de: Third conditional (if + past perfect, would have)
grammar_rules.explanation_de: Irreale Bedingung in der Vergangenheit: If I had known, I would have helped you.
grammar_rules.example_positive: If I had known about the party, I would have come.
grammar_rules.example_negative: If I know about the party, I will come.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: used to + Infinitiv für Gewohnheiten und Zustände, die es nicht mehr gibt: I used to live in Berlin. Nicht verwechseln mit be used to + -ing (gewohnt sein).
grammar_rules.example_positive: I used to play the piano when I was a child.
grammar_rules.example_negative: I am used to getting up early.

grammar_rules.explanation_de: wish + past simple für Gegenwart (I wish I had more time), wish + past perfect für Vergangenheit (I wish I had studied harder).
grammar_rules.example_positive: I wish I had more free time.
grammar_rules.example_negative: I hope I have more free time.

common_errors.wrong_example: We need to discuss about the budget.
common_errors.correct_example: We need to discuss the budget.
common_errors.explanation_de: discuss steht direkt mit Objekt: discuss the budget. Mit about nur das Nomen: a discussion about the budget, oder talk about.

common_errors.title_de: explain me statt explain to me
common_errors.suggestion_es: explain something to me / explain to me how …
common_errors.wrong_example: Can you explain me the problem?
common_errors.correct_example: Can you explain the problem to me?
common_errors.explanation_de: explain hat kein indirektes Objekt ohne Präposition: explain something to someone (anders als „jemandem etwas erklären“).

common_errors.wrong_example: Many people is interested in this topic.
common_errors.correct_example: Many people are interested in this topic.
common_errors.explanation_de: people ist im Englischen Plural: people are, people have. Lernende übertragen oft den Singular von „man“ oder „das Volk“.

common_errors.title_de: Präsens statt Present perfect mit since
common_errors.suggestion_es: Present perfect: I have lived here since 2020.
common_errors.correct_example: I have lived in Hamburg since 2019.
common_errors.explanation_de: Dauert etwas seit einem Zeitpunkt bis jetzt an, steht im Englischen das Present perfect, nicht das Präsens wie im Deutschen („ich wohne seit 2019 hier“): I have lived here since 2019.

common_errors.title_de: since statt for bei einer Zeitdauer
common_errors.wrong_example: I have lived here since two years.
common_errors.correct_example: I have lived here for two years.
common_errors.explanation_de: Deutsches „seit“ hat zwei Entsprechungen: for + Zeitraum (for two years), since + Zeitpunkt (since 2020, since Monday).

common_errors.suggestion_es: information, advice, furniture (ohne -s); pieces of advice
common_errors.wrong_example: Thank you for all the informations.
common_errors.correct_example: Thank you for all the information.
common_errors.explanation_de: information, advice, furniture, equipment, knowledge, homework, luggage und research sind im Englischen unzählbar: kein -s, kein a/an. Für Einzelstücke: a piece of advice.

common_errors.suggestion_es: if + past: If I had …, I would …
common_errors.wrong_example: If I would have more time, I would learn Japanese.
common_errors.correct_example: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
common_errors.explanation_de: Im if-Satz steht kein would (anders als im Deutschen „wenn ich … würde“): If I had more time … Höfliche Bitten wie „if you would like“ oder „if you would be so kind“ sind richtig.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die richtige Form.
exercises.source_text_es: This flat is ___ than the one we saw yesterday.

accepted_answers.text: cheaper

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Kurze Adjektive steigert man mit -er: cheaper.
„cheapest“ ist der Superlativ; mit „than“ steht der Komparativ.
Vor „than“ steht der Komparativ: cheaper.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze „go“ in der passenden Form.
exercises.source_text_es: Last summer we ___ to Scotland for two weeks.

accepted_answers.text: went

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Ein abgeschlossener Zeitpunkt (last summer) verlangt das past simple: we went.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die richtige Form.
exercises.source_text_es: Thank you for all the useful ___.

accepted_answers.text: information

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „information“ ist unzählbar: kein -s.
Unzählbar: kein a/an. Einzelstück: a piece of information.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze „be“ in der passenden Form.
exercises.source_text_es: Many people ___ interested in this topic.

accepted_answers.text: are

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „people“ ist Plural: people are.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze die Passivform von „build“.
exercises.source_text_es: The museum was ___ in the nineteenth century.

accepted_answers.text: built

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „build“ ist unregelmäßig: built.

exercises.prompt_de: Forme den Satz ins Passiv um.
exercises.source_text_es: They sold the house last year.
exercises.instruction_de: be (in der Zeit des Aktivsatzes) + Partizip.

accepted_answers.text: The house was sold last year.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze das passende Hilfsverb (Dauer bis heute).
exercises.source_text_es: I ___ lived in Hamburg since 2019.

accepted_answers.text: have
've

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Dauer bis jetzt mit since: present perfect, I have lived.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze das Partizip von „see“.
exercises.source_text_es: I have never ___ such a beautiful view.

accepted_answers.text: seen

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Nach „have“ steht das Partizip: seen.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die richtige Präposition.
exercises.source_text_es: She has worked here ___ three years.

accepted_answers.text: for

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Zeitraum → for (for three years); Zeitpunkt → since (since Monday).
„during“ heißt „während“ (during the meeting).
Dauer bis jetzt: for three years.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle das passende Relativpronomen.
exercises.source_text_es: That's the woman ___ son plays in our team.

accepted_answers.text: whose

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Besitz (ihr Sohn): whose.
„which“ steht für Dinge; Besitz: whose.
„whom“ ist Objekt (the woman whom I met); Besitz: whose.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze „have“ in der passenden Form.
exercises.source_text_es: If I ___ more money, I would travel around the world.

accepted_answers.text: had

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Im if-Satz steht kein would: If I had …

exercises.prompt_de: Mach aus der realen Bedingung eine Hypothese.
exercises.source_text_es: If I have time, I will help you.
exercises.instruction_de: if + past simple, im Hauptsatz would.

accepted_answers.text: If I had time, I would help you.
If I had time, I'd help you.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze die Form für eine frühere Gewohnheit.
exercises.source_text_es: When I was a child, I used to ___ the piano every day.

accepted_answers.text: play

wrong_answers.feedback_de: used to + Infinitiv (frühere Gewohnheit). „be used to + -ing“ heißt „gewohnt sein“.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die passende Form (früher, heute nicht mehr).
exercises.source_text_es: We ___ live in London, but now we live in Leeds.

accepted_answers.text: used to

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „be used to“ heißt „gewohnt sein“ und steht mit -ing.
Im Aussagesatz: used to (nur nach did/didn't: use to).
„were used to“ heißt „waren gewohnt“.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die passende Vermutung über die Vergangenheit.
exercises.source_text_es: The lights are off. They ___ gone to bed already.

accepted_answers.text: must have

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Vermutung über die Vergangenheit: must have + Partizip.
„should gone“ ist ungrammatisch; Vermutung: must have gone.
„have to“ drückt Pflicht aus, keine Vermutung.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze das Partizip von „tell“ (Kritik an der Vergangenheit).
exercises.source_text_es: You should have ___ me earlier.

accepted_answers.text: told

wrong_answers.feedback_de: should have + Partizip: should have told.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze das passende Hilfsverb (Vorvergangenheit).
exercises.source_text_es: When we arrived, the film ___ already started.

accepted_answers.text: had

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Vor einem vergangenen Ereignis (we arrived): past perfect, had started.

exercises.prompt_de: Gib den Satz in indirekter Rede wieder: She said …
exercises.source_text_es: "I am very tired," she said.

accepted_answers.text: She said she was very tired.
She said that she was very tired.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die passende Form.
exercises.source_text_es: If I had known about the party, I ___ come.

accepted_answers.text: would have

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Irreale Vergangenheit: would have + Partizip (would have come).
„will have“ ist futur II; hier irreal: would have.
Im Hauptsatz der third conditional: would have.

exercises.prompt_de: Drücke das Bedauern als irreale Bedingung aus.
exercises.source_text_es: I didn't study, so I failed the exam.
exercises.instruction_de: If + past perfect, would have + Partizip.

accepted_answers.text: If I had studied, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied, I wouldn't have failed the exam.
If I had studied, I would not have failed the exam.

exercises.prompt_de: Ergänze „have“ in der passenden Form.
exercises.source_text_es: I wish I ___ more free time.

accepted_answers.text: had

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Nach „I wish“ steht für die Gegenwart das past simple: I wish I had.

exercises.prompt_de: Hebe hervor, was du brauchst: Beginne mit „What I …“.
exercises.source_text_es: I really need a long holiday.

accepted_answers.text: What I really need is a long holiday.

exercises.prompt_de: Formuliere die Behauptung vorsichtiger (akademischer Stil).
exercises.source_text_es: Remote work increases productivity.
exercises.instruction_de: Verwende eine abschwächende Wendung (it could be argued that …, to some extent …).

accepted_answers.text: It could be argued that remote work increases productivity.
Remote work arguably increases productivity.
To some extent, remote work increases productivity.
Remote work is likely to increase productivity.

exercises.prompt_de: Beginne den Satz mit „Not only“.
exercises.source_text_es: She won the race and she also broke the record.
exercises.instruction_de: Nach „Not only“ am Satzanfang folgt Fragewortstellung (did she …).

accepted_answers.text: Not only did she win the race, she also broke the record.
Not only did she win the race, but she also broke the record.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die richtige Wortstellung.
exercises.source_text_es: Rarely ___ such a talented young player.

accepted_answers.text: have I seen

wrong_answers.feedback_de: Nach „Rarely“ am Satzanfang folgt Inversion: Rarely have I seen …
Nach einschränkendem Ausdruck am Satzanfang: Hilfsverb vor dem Subjekt.
Das Hilfsverb steht vor dem Subjekt, das Partizip danach: have I seen.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle die passende Form (vergangene Bedingung, heutige Folge).
exercises.source_text_es: If I had taken that job, I ___ in Tokyo now.

accepted_answers.text: would be living

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „now“ zeigt eine Folge in der Gegenwart: would be (living).
Irreale Folge: would, nicht will.
Im Hauptsatz steht would.

exercises.prompt_de: Formuliere im Nominalstil (akademisch).
exercises.source_text_es: Because prices increased sharply, demand fell.
exercises.instruction_de: Ersetze den because-Satz durch eine Nominalgruppe (due to / owing to …).

accepted_answers.text: Due to the sharp increase in prices, demand fell.
Owing to the sharp increase in prices, demand fell.
The sharp increase in prices led to a fall in demand.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle das präziseste Verb.
exercises.source_text_es: Cutting the budget for public transport would only ___ the traffic problems in the city.

accepted_answers.text: exacerbate

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „mitigate“ heißt abmildern; Kürzungen verschlimmern die Probleme.
„comply with“ heißt einhalten (Regeln).
„alleviate“ heißt lindern, das Gegenteil des Gemeinten.

exercises.prompt_de: Wähle das präziseste Verb (formeller Bericht).
exercises.source_text_es: The new regulations are intended to ___ the environmental impact of air travel.

accepted_answers.text: mitigate

wrong_answers.feedback_de: „exacerbate“ heißt verschlimmern, das Gegenteil des Gemeinten.
„undermine“ heißt untergraben, schwächen (eine Autorität, ein Vertrauen).
„scrutinise“ heißt genau prüfen.

exercises.prompt_de: Formuliere die Nachricht formell (Brief an einen Kunden).

exercises.instruction_de: Bedauern formell ausdrücken (We regret to inform you …), keine Kurzformen.

accepted_answers.text: We regret to inform you that we are unable to offer you a refund.

exercises.source_text_es: It has become fashionable to blame smartphones for a supposed collapse in our ability to concentrate. The argument is seductive in its simplicity: apps are engineered to capture our attention, and every notification chips away at our capacity for sustained thought. Yet the evidence is rather more ambiguous than the headlines suggest. Studies of attention span are notoriously difficult to compare, and some of the most frequently quoted figures turn out to have no traceable source at all. This is not to say that the design of digital products is harmless; it is to suggest that the problem may lie less in our brains than in the environments we have built around them. If that is the case, the remedy is not a nostalgic retreat from technology but a deliberate effort to design spaces, both digital and physical, that reward depth rather than distraction.

texts.title_es: On Liberty: "On the contrary, even opinions lose…"
texts.body_es: On the contrary, even opinions lose their immunity, when the circumstances in which they are expressed are such as to constitute their expression a positive instigation to some mischievous act. An opinion that corn-dealers are starvers of the poor, or that private property is robbery, ought to be unmolested when simply circulated through the press, but may justly incur punishment when delivered orally to an excited mob assembled before the house of a corn-dealer, or when handed about among the same mob in the form of a placard. texts.title_es: On Liberty: "No one's idea of excellence in…"
texts.body_es: No one's idea of excellence in conduct is that people should do absolutely nothing but copy one another. No one would assert that people ought not to put into their mode of life, and into the conduct of their concerns, any impress whatever of their own judgment, or of their own individual character. On the other hand, it would be absurd to pretend that people ought to live as if nothing whatever had been known in the world before they came into it; as if experience had as yet done nothing towards showing that one mode of existence, or of conduct, is preferable to another. Nobody denies that people should be so taught and trained in youth, as to know and benefit by the ascertained results of human experience. But it is the privilege and proper condition of a human being, arrived at the maturity of his faculties, to use and interpret experience in his own way.

texts.title_es: On Liberty: "He who lets the world, or…"
texts.body_es: He who lets the world, or his own portion of it, choose his plan of life for him, has no need of any other faculty than the ape-like one of imitation. He who chooses his plan for himself, employs all his faculties. He must use observation to see, reasoning and judgment to foresee, activity to gather materials for decision, discrimination to decide, and when he has decided, firmness and self-control to hold to his deliberate decision. And these qualities he requires and exercises exactly in proportion as the part of his conduct which he determines according to his own judgment and feelings is a large one.

texts.body_es: It has become fashionable to blame smartphones for a supposed collapse in our ability to concentrate. The argument is seductive in its simplicity: apps are engineered to capture our attention, and every notification chips away at our capacity for sustained thought. Yet the evidence is rather more ambiguous than the headlines suggest. Studies of attention span are notoriously difficult to compare, and some of the most frequently quoted figures turn out to have no traceable source at all. This is not to say that the design of digital products is harmless; it is to suggest that the problem may lie less in our brains than in the environments we have built around them. If that is the case, the remedy is not a nostalgic retreat from technology but a deliberate effort to design spaces, both digital and physical, that reward depth rather than distraction.

localizations.title: discuss about en lugar de discuss
localizations.explanation: discuss lleva el objeto directamente: discuss the budget. Con about solo el sustantivo: a discussion about the budget, o bien talk about.

localizations.title: explain me en lugar de explain to me
localizations.explanation: explain no admite objeto indirecto sin preposición: explain something to someone (a diferencia de „explicarle algo a alguien“).

localizations.title: people con el verbo en singular
localizations.explanation: En inglés people es plural: people are, people have. Se suele trasladar el singular de „la gente“ o „das Volk“.

localizations.title: Presente en lugar de present perfect con since
localizations.explanation: Si algo dura desde un momento hasta ahora, en inglés se usa el present perfect, no el presente como en alemán o en español („vivo aquí desde 2019“): I have lived here since 2019.

localizations.title: since en lugar de for con una duración
localizations.explanation: „Desde“/„seit“ tiene dos equivalentes: for + período (for two years), since + momento (since 2020, since Monday).

localizations.title: Plural de sustantivos incontables (informations, advices)
localizations.explanation: information, advice, furniture, equipment, knowledge, homework, luggage y research son incontables en inglés: sin -s y sin a/an. Para una unidad: a piece of advice.

localizations.title: would en la oración con if
localizations.explanation: En la oración con if no va would (a diferencia del alemán „wenn ich … würde“): If I had more time … Las peticiones corteses como „if you would like“ o „if you would be so kind“ son correctas.

localizations.title: Oraciones escindidas (What I need is …)
localizations.explanation: Énfasis con una oración con what o con all: What I need is a holiday. All I want is some peace.

localizations.title: Comparativo y superlativo
localizations.explanation: Adjetivos cortos con -er/-est (cheaper, the cheapest), largos con more/most (more expensive). La comparación, con than.

localizations.title: Contabilidad y concordancia (people are, information)
localizations.explanation: Los sustantivos incontables no tienen plural (information, advice, furniture); people y police van con el verbo en plural (people are).

localizations.title: Matizar (hedging)
localizations.explanation: Formular afirmaciones con cautela: It could be argued that …, to some extent, arguably, it seems that …, tend to.

localizations.title: Inversión tras expresiones restrictivas
localizations.explanation: Al principio de la frase, después de never, rarely, not only, no sooner, under no circumstances …, se usa el orden de la pregunta: Not only did she win, she also broke the record.

localizations.title: Condicional mixto
localizations.explanation: Condición pasada, consecuencia presente: If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.

localizations.title: Verbo modal + have + participio (must have, should have)
localizations.explanation: Suposición o crítica sobre el pasado: She must have forgotten. You should have told me. They might have missed the bus.

localizations.title: Nominalización (estilo académico)
localizations.explanation: Verbos y adjetivos se convierten en sustantivos: because prices increased → due to the increase in prices; it is important → the importance of.

localizations.title: Pasiva
localizations.explanation: be + participio: lo importante es la acción. The bridge was built in 1890. English is spoken here. El agente va con by.

localizations.title: Past perfect
localizations.explanation: had + participio: lo que ocurrió antes de otro hecho pasado. When we arrived, the film had already started.

localizations.title: Past simple
localizations.explanation: Acción terminada en un momento concreto: I went to London last year. Preguntas y negación con did: Did you see it? I didn't see it.

localizations.title: Present perfect
localizations.explanation: have/has + participio: experiencias y acciones relacionadas con el presente (I have been to Rome. She has just left). Con since/for para una duración hasta ahora.

localizations.title: Cambio de registro
localizations.explanation: Expresar el mismo contenido de forma formal e informal: We regret to inform you … ↔ Sorry, but …

localizations.title: Oraciones de relativo (who, which, that, whose)
localizations.explanation: who para personas, which para cosas, that para ambas en las oraciones de relativo especificativas; whose para la posesión. Las explicativas van con coma y sin that.

localizations.title: Estilo indirecto con cambio de tiempo
localizations.explanation: Después de said/told/asked el tiempo verbal suele retroceder: She said she was tired. He told me he would call.

localizations.title: Second conditional (if + past, would)
localizations.explanation: Condición hipotética en el presente: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese. En la oración con if no va would.

localizations.title: Precisión estilística
localizations.explanation: La palabra exacta en lugar de una general: mitigate en vez de make smaller, scrutinise en vez de look at, exacerbate en vez de make worse.

localizations.title: Third conditional (if + past perfect, would have)
localizations.explanation: Condición irreal en el pasado: If I had known, I would have helped you.

localizations.title: used to (costumbre pasada)
localizations.explanation: used to + infinitivo para costumbres y estados que ya no existen: I used to live in Berlin. No confundir con be used to + -ing (estar acostumbrado).

localizations.title: wish + past (lamento)
localizations.explanation: wish + past simple para el presente (I wish I had more time), wish + past perfect para el pasado (I wish I had studied harder).
